text:
Catawba County News

BOC Recap: 11/2/26

Published: November 03, 2026

The November 2, 2026, Catawba County Board of Commissioners meeting was called to order at 7 p.m. The agenda for the meeting can be found at https://bit.ly/3utv5SE.

BOC approved minutes from the Board’s Regular Meeting and Closed Session of October 19, 2026.

Appointments Commissioner Abernethy recommends the following appointments to the Catawba Valley Medical Center Board of Trustees: Debra Bechtel to a first full term; Summer McGee and Randy Isenhower to first terms, beginning January 1, 2027, with term expirations of December 31, 2030.

Presentations

Commissioner Setzer presented a proclamation in observance of Operation Green Light in support of veterans.

Public Hearings

1 – Public hearing to consider adoption of the proposed Schedule of Values, Standards and Rules for the 2027 Property Revaluation as prescribed by North Carolina General Statute §105-317.

BACKGROUND

Pursuant to a resolution adopted by the Board of Commissioners on September 18, 2023, Catawba County's next countywide revaluation will become effective January 1, 2027. Catawba County has approximately 95,000 parcels of land, all of which are required by state law to be appraised at 100% of market value as of the effective date of the revaluation. BOC will consider approval at Nov. 16 meeting.

2 - Public hearing to consider adoption of a resolution declaring Catawba County’s participation in the Commercial Property Assessed Capital Expenditure (C-PACE) Program.

BACKGROUND

The NC Commercial Property Assessed Capital Expenditure (C-PACE) Program offers long-term private financing for commercial property upgrades in energy, water, and resiliency improvements. Established by the General Assembly in 2024 through Senate Bill 802, C-PACE is administered by the Economic Development Partnership of NC. The program creates an additional financing tool for property owners to use private funds to finance improvements to eligible properties, supporting economic development by helping building owners make major building improvements, refinance / recapitalize after improvements, construct new buildings, and drive jobs and investment. BOC approved.

3 - Public hearing to consider adoption of the proposed resolution approving an Economic Development Agreement between Catawba County and Utili-Serve, LLC and CLD Land, LLC, and authorize the Chair to execute these along with any other needed documents.

BACKGROUND

Founded in 2008, Utili-Serve is a privately held utility infrastructure services company headquartered in Conover that offers a range of specialized services in the electric power industry, including turnkey substation construction and maintenance, transformer and apparatus work, and nuclear/general construction. The company operates 30 specialized construction crews and maintains three locations in Conover, Raleigh, and Greenville, SC. The company is evaluating a multi-state expansion to support accelerating demand for electric grid modernization, transmission upgrades, and storm resiliency infrastructure across the Southeast. BOC approved.

Consent Agenda

1 – The Finance and Personnel Subcommittee requests the Board of Commissioners appropriate $235,000 in Public Health restricted revenues to maintain continuity in community-based pregnancy and birth outcome care management services through the fiscal year.

2 – The Finance and Personnel Subcommittee requests the Board of Commissioners reallocate $95,235.64 in ARPA funding to similar ARPA eligible projects previously obligated before the obligation deadline of December 31, 2024, and revise the ARPA Grant Ordinance to reflect the transfer appropriation.

3 – Staff requests the Board of Commissioners conduct a second reading and consider adopting proposed revisions to Chapter 32 – Solid Waste of the Catawba County Code of Ordinances, which inserts the entire Abandoned and Junk Vehicles section of regulations previously included in the Unified Development Ordinance.

BACKGROUND

On October 19, 2026 the Board of Commissioners adopted an update to the County’s Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). The previous version of the UDO included a section on code enforcement rules and regulations related to Abandoned and Junk Vehicles. Through the UDO update process, the decision was made to relocate this entire section from the UDO to the County Code of Ordinances. There are no substantive changes proposed to the content of the regulations; this is just a reorganization of where this chapter fits into the overarching County regulatory framework.

BOC approved all three items.

Manager’s Report

None

Adjournment

BOC adjourned the meeting at 7:47 p.m.

The deal gives Canadian fleet operators local sales and service for the W56 Class 5-6 electric van, with expansion to Western Canada planned

Workhorse Group has signed an agreement with Tristan Fleet Management to sell and service its electric step vans in Canada, a major step for the Detroit-based technology company inking its first Canadian dealer partnership.

Under the contract, Tristan will offer Workhorse’s full W56 lineup with two battery options: a standard 210 kilowatt-hour pack with a range of up to 240 km, and a less expensive 140 kWh version. Two configurations for the vans – 178-inch or 208-inch wheelbases – offer 1,000 cubic feet and 1,200 cubic feet of cargo space respectively, with payload capacity ranging from 9,000 lbs to 11,000 pounds.

Sales and service

Tristan is primarily known for helping carriers and fleet operators maintain and service heavy trucks and trailers, but they also began to sell transit trailers through partnerships with firms such as Vanguard.

For the past year, Workhorse has been looking to expand its reach to Canadian fleet managers. “When we wanted to scale up operations in Canada, we needed a support system for our products,” said David Bellitto, the country director of Canada for Workhorse, in an interview with Electric Autonomy. “Because the EV market isn’t just about buying a great vehicle, it’s giving drivers the service and support they want.”

He went on to say how Tristan’s track record made it an easy decision for Workhorse. “We wanted a local presence, and they have that local presence in Canada.

“We look forward to growing beyond Ontario towards Western Canada in the coming years, too,” Bellitto added.

Strong business case for electrifying

For Tristan, this partnership built off its commitment to working with more EV manufacturers. “Our customers have been exploring electrification for some time now. With generous incentives from Écocamionnage [Quebec’s electric MHDV rebate program], as well as the current extremely high cost of fuel, the business case for going electric has never been stronger,” Daniel Barbu, Tristan’s vice-president and general manager, said in a press release.

“We’re looking forward to helping Workhorse expand its customer base across Canada and supporting our customers [to] meet their own goals for sustainability and vehicle performance.”

This deal isn’t Workhorse’s first foray into Canada. It has been operating in the country since 2021 through a partnership with Purolator, which also recently placed an additional order for 100 electric vans in March.

📣 Spread the word about climate change. Share this newsletter with friends!

As Americans wait for the results of today’s midterm elections, one thing is certain: Former Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell, who until recently wielded extraordinary power over U.S. climate policy, will not return to the Senate after this session. The 84-year-old senator has experienced health problems and did not seek reelection. Today, Dana Nuccitelli offers this analysis of McConnell’s impact on federal efforts to tackle climate change.

– Sara Peach, Editor-in-Chief

Mitch McConnell’s climate legacy

Dana Nuccitelli reports:

Outgoing Sen. Mitch McConnell was one of the most powerful figures ever to walk the halls of the U.S. Congress and was instrumental in steering the country’s climate policy. At virtually every opportunity, he chose to block efforts to address the problem.

McConnell, a Republican from Kentucky, is set to retire from the Senate in January. At that point, he will have been the 10th-longest-serving senator in U.S. history. He was also the longest-serving Senate party leader in history.

During his tenure, McConnell exerted his power to halt or overturn climate action in Congress, at the Supreme Court, and in the White House. Over a decades-long career, he joined a short list of individuals most responsible for stymying political efforts to address climate change.

Opposition to cap-and-trade

Over his 40-year tenure in the Senate, McConnell received over $4 million in donations from the oil and gas and coal industries – the fifth-most of any senator.

He was chosen as the leader of Senate Republicans in 2007, shortly before President Barack Obama, a Democrat, won office. At the time, observers thought it possible that Congress would pass bipartisan legislation to combat climate change. In 2008, Democratic House leader Nancy Pelosi and former Republican House leader Newt Gingrich had created an ad together in which Gingrich said, “We do agree: Our country must take action to address climate change.”

The House soon passed a carbon cap-and-trade bill designed to tackle climate pollution. Eight Republicans voted in favor.

The late Sen. Lindsey Graham, a Republican, was one of the leaders of drafting a Senate version of the cap-and-trade bill. But rather than support the legislation, McConnell decided instead to declare war on Obama’s entire agenda, as reporter Ryan Lizza documented in a 2010 article. By working on a climate bill, Republican senators risked angering McConnell.

The cap-and-trade bill died a quiet death, never having received a vote in the Senate.

In 2019, McConnell acknowledged the reality of human-caused climate change. At the time, he said he preferred to solve the problem through technology and innovation. Yet he opposed legislation that climate advocates and researchers said would spur technological innovation, such as a price on carbon pollution and clean energy tax credits.

The Senate eventually passed sweeping climate legislation in 2022, when Democrats enacted the Inflation Reduction Act. McConnell vehemently opposed the bill.

In 2025, McConnell helped to repeal many provisions of the Inflation Reduction Act when he supported the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which passed the Senate by a single vote.

McConnell’s conservative Supreme Court

The senator expressed pride in his influence over the Supreme Court. Notably, he blocked Obama’s nomination of moderate Merrick Garland in 2016 to replace Justice Antonin Scalia. In a move that broke with norms and historical precedent, McConnell refused to allow the chamber to consider or vote on Garland’s nomination.

“The most important decision I’ve made in my entire political career was not to fill the Supreme Court vacancy when Justice Scalia passed away,” McConnell recalled in 2024.

Soon after taking office in January 2017, Trump nominated the conservative Neil Gorsuch to the court, and the Republican-controlled Senate approved him. The Senate under McConnell also approved the 2018 nomination of conservative Brett Kavanaugh and the 2020 nomination of conservative Amy Coney Barrett.

Under conservative control, the court has consistently issued rulings that undermine climate and other environmental regulations, including decisions that could enable the Supreme Court to block federal climate regulations in the future.

A crucial vote to acquit

In January 2021, the senator had an opportunity to prevent a second Trump administration. He chose not to take it.

The House of Representatives had impeached Trump for inciting an insurrection at the Capitol a week earlier.

“There’s no question that President Trump is practically and morally responsible for provoking the events of the day,” McConnell said at the time.

But he declined to whip his caucus to remove Trump. Instead, McConnell and 42 other Republican senators voted to acquit him.

Had Trump been impeached, he would have been constitutionally barred from ever again holding office. Instead, he was elected to a second term in 2024 and has presided over the most anti-climate-policy administration in U.S. history, which has included withdrawing from the Paris climate agreement for the second time and repealing virtually all federal climate policies. It proved to be a fitting capstone to McConnell’s lengthy career of sabotaging climate policy at every level of government.

description:
Previous blog posts in this series discussed how the rollback of greenhouse gas standards that regulated light-duty vehicles and power plants affect costs, increase greenhouse gas emissions, and contribute to climate-related economic damages.
In this blog post, we complete the picture by providing estimates of the forgone air quality–related health benefits resulting from those rollbacks.
Based on our estimates for the rollback of the power plant greenhouse gas standards, the dollar value of forgone health benefits alone is more than double EPA’s estimated cost savings.
This figure shows the impact of the finalized rollback of the light-duty vehicle greenhouse gas standards alone, as well as the combined impact of the rollbacks of the greenhouse gas and criteria pollutant standards.

text:
Previous blog posts in this series discussed how the rollback of greenhouse gas standards that regulated light-duty vehicles and power plants affect costs, increase greenhouse gas emissions, and contribute to climate-related economic damages. In this blog post, we complete the picture by providing estimates of the forgone air quality–related health benefits resulting from those rollbacks.

Eliminating these greenhouse gas standards changes the nation’s light-duty fleet and electric power sector, which in turn directly affect the emissions of traditional air pollutants, including sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometers or smaller (PM2.5). The potential rollback or significant weakening of vehicle criteria pollutant standards announced by EPA in May 2026 would further increase pollution.

Changes in emissions of traditional air pollutants affect ambient concentrations of ozone and PM2.5. Ambient concentrations of these two pollutants cause a wide range of human health effects including premature death, hospitalization, asthma exacerbation, and respiratory and cardiovascular illnesses. They also contribute to acid rain and other environmental harms.

The effect of emissions on air quality is complex. Emitted pollutants affect the ambient air quality of people directly downwind of emitting sources, but can also react with other pollutants and, transported by the wind, affect the air quality of people many hundreds of miles away.

Our modeling shows that the finalized and proposed rollbacks will significantly increase PM2.5 and ozone pollution, causing 95,000 premature deaths between 2032 and 2050. Hospital visits, chronic diseases, and lost work and school days also result from the increase in pollution. These mortality and morbidity impacts are concentrated in the US Midwest and East.

Based on our estimates for the rollback of the power plant greenhouse gas standards, the dollar value of forgone health benefits alone is more than double EPA’s estimated cost savings. For the combined rollback of both power plant and vehicle greenhouse gas standards, when climate-related damages are added in (which we calculated in previous blog posts in this series), the dollar value of forgone air quality and climate benefits exceeds cost savings by over five times, or over $3.4 trillion.

Air Pollution Rises Substantially Due to Rollbacks of the Standards

As in previous analyses, we used Resources for the Future’s light-duty Vehicle Market Model and Engineering, Economic, and Environmental Electricity Simulation Tool to estimate changes in emissions associated with the rollbacks of the light-duty vehicle greenhouse gas standards and the Section 111(d) greenhouse gas standards for fossil fuel–powered electricity generation.

We also evaluate the potential impacts of EPA’s announced plans to reconsider the Tier 4 criteria pollutant standards for light-duty vehicles. We estimate how the proposed and finalized rollbacks change emissions by comparing regulatory rollback scenarios to a baseline that includes the repeal of elements of the Inflation Reduction Act and Good Neighbor Plan, and an expected increasing demand for electricity. We take an incremental approach to estimating the impact of the rollbacks, starting by comparing the rollback of the light-duty vehicle greenhouse gas standards to the baseline and then estimating the additional impact of also rolling back the power plant standards or vehicle criteria pollutant standards. In our upcoming report, we explored the impacts of these rollbacks using an additional baseline with lower energy demand, which approximates what the future would look like in the absence of rapid data center growth.

Figure 1 shows the projected changes to vehicle-related emissions from 2032 to 2050. This figure shows the impact of the finalized rollback of the light-duty vehicle greenhouse gas standards alone, as well as the combined impact of the rollbacks of the greenhouse gas and criteria pollutant standards. Even though manufacturers no longer have to comply with the greenhouse gas standards, we modeled the scenarios to exclude backsliding; manufacturers in our model do not reduce fuel economy nor sell fewer plug-in vehicles than in 2025.

Figure 1. Changes in Emissions of Air Pollutants Resulting from Rollbacks of Greenhouse Gas and Criteria Pollutant Standards for Vehicles

The difference between the two lines is the incremental impact of rolling back the criteria pollutant standards after the rollback of the greenhouse gas standards. This incremental change has a large impact on nitrogen oxide and PM2.5 emissions because they are primarily tailpipe emissions directly controlled by the criteria pollutant standards. By contrast, sulfur dioxide emissions from the combined rollbacks are largely due to the increase in refinery emissions resulting from the rollback of the greenhouse gas standards, which we project to increase diesel and gasoline consumption to a much higher degree than the rollback in criteria pollutant standards.

Figure 2 shows the projected changes in pollutant levels from the rollback of the power plant standards, which projects greater use of higher-emitting fossil fuel generation to meet electricity demands.

Figure 2. Change in Emissions of Air Pollutants Resulting from the Rollback of the Greenhouse Gas Standards for Power Plants

We apply a simplified approach to estimate air quality developed by EPA called the Pattern Constructed Air Pollution Surfaces method. This method translates county-level emissions of PM2.5, nitrogen oxide, sulfur dioxide, and volatile organic compounds from vehicles, refineries, and power plants into annual average ambient PM2.5 and seasonal ozone concentrations for each county in the continental United States.

Our air-quality modeling shows that the combined regulatory rollbacks will have widespread impacts on ozone and PM2.5 across the United States, with the greatest impacts in the Midwest and East, where fossil fuel–fired generation is highest, and in and around counties where refineries are located, especially in Texas, Louisiana, and California.

Figure 3 shows the spatial patterns of changes in ambient average annual PM2.5 (top-left panel) and seasonal ozone concentrations (top-right panel) in 2050. This figure shows the changes between the baseline and the combination of rollbacks of the vehicle greenhouse gas standards, criteria pollutant standards, and the power plant greenhouse gas standards.

We estimate that the increases in ambient PM2.5 and ozone from these rollbacks will result in a substantial number of excess premature deaths nationwide. Relative to the baseline, the finalized rollbacks of the vehicle and power plant greenhouse gas standards and potential rollback of the vehicle criteria pollutant standards cause 4,300 to 5,300 PM2.5- and ozone-attributable deaths per year between 2032 and 2050, for a cumulative total of about 95,000 premature deaths over this period.

During these years, we also estimate chronic and acute morbidity impacts from changes in air quality. PM2.5-related morbidities include

43,000 hospital and emergency department visits;

1,300 heart attacks;

2,300 strokes;

2,500 cases of Parkinson’s disease;

24,000 cases of Alzheimer’s disease;

2,800 cases of lung cancer;

4.3 million days of lost work;

17 million cases of aggravated asthma; and

25 million cases of acute respiratory symptoms.

Ozone-related morbidities over the same time period include

36,000 hospital and emergency department visits;

7.3 million days of lost school; and

20 million cases of aggravated asthma.

The estimated number of annual and cumulative premature deaths, broken out by regulation, is shown in Figure 4. The number of premature deaths caused by the vehicle standard rollbacks increases over time. Premature deaths from rolling back power plant standards increase through 2040 and then fall slightly by 2050 due to the retirements of coal-fired plants. Morbidity effects display similar trends to mortality effects.

description:

There is also a move to try and reduce smog caused by delivery vehicles.
In late October, Amazon and Tata Motors announced a collaboration that will see 3,000 electric trucks delivered to the retail giant’s delivery partners.
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility Another OEM which has made moves to support uptake of electrified vehicles is Mahindra.
The Mahindra Last Mile Mobility (MLMM) program has leveraged the company supply chain to help support greater sales of electric three-wheeler delivery vehicles.
text:
New Delhi, capital of India, has one of the worst air pollution problems of any city in the world.

The smog is caused by a series of compounding issues, including fires used to clear fields and coal-fired power plants, together with the millions of fossil-fuel powered vehicles travelling across the city every day.

This is worsend by winter conditions that can cause a temperature inversion which traps a layer of pollution closer the ground.

Under the Winter Action Plan, authorities in New Delhi have rolled out a series of measures to help address vehicle pollution, including a doubling of parking fees, fines for non-compliant vehicles and a mandated 50% work-from-home order for government and private offices.

There is also a move to try and reduce smog caused by delivery vehicles. In late October, Amazon and Tata Motors announced a collaboration that will see 3,000 electric trucks delivered to the retail giant’s delivery partners.

Many of these will be the Tata Ultra E.7, a truck model which features CCS2 fast charging, regenerative braking and a series of high-voltage safety systems.

With a launch timed to match the busy festive season, the trucks will be used as middle-mile transportation supporting package transfers. There are also plans to electrify the Delhi-Bengal-Chennai corridor, India’s busiest route that crosses seven states.

The launch comes after the introduction of Delhi’s 2026 EV Policy, which will give the first 1,000 privately-owned medium duty electric trucks registered in the first three months after the policy comes into effect unlimited access to city centres for a full 10 years – bypassing the ‘No Entry’ hours.

Mahindra Last Mile Mobility

Another OEM which has made moves to support uptake of electrified vehicles is Mahindra. The Mahindra Last Mile Mobility (MLMM) program has leveraged the company supply chain to help support greater sales of electric three-wheeler delivery vehicles.

Named as a finalist in The Earthshot Prize 2026, a global environmental awards program founded by HRH Prince William, the goal is to show that the company can deliver electric vehicles responsibly and profitably.

To date, Mahindra says that is has sold more than 400,000 electric last-mile delivery vehicles that have together stopped an estimated 180,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions from reaching the atmosphere.

These include the Mahindra Treo Zor and Zor Grand. These three-wheelers cargo vehicles use a 48 V system with 10.24 kWh li-ion batteries that power either an 8 kW or 12 kW motor. Single-charge range across the two can vary from 80 to 120 km. Maximum payload capacity is up to 500 kg.

In addition, the MLMM has related customer support initiatives including accident insurance and financial counselling.

description:
Consolidated revenue from automotive and software & services was US$2.155 billion, up 38% from the same quarter of last year.
Revenues from software & services, such as subscription fees, were US$605 million, up 45% on the prior year’s Q3.

Software and services gross profit for the third quarter was US$256 million, a 42% margin and US$102 million improvement over Q3 2025.
Regarding our technology roadmap, our autonomy platform is progressing rapidly, and we are super excited about Point to Point.
text:
EV manufacturer Rivian Automotive has announced its third quarter 2026 financial results.

The company shipped nearly 20,000 vehicles from its manufacturing facility in Normal, Illinois in Q3, and has revised its unit delivery prediction for the rest of the year to between 67,000 to 70,000 vehicles.

Consolidated revenue from automotive and software & services was US$2.155 billion, up 38% from the same quarter of last year. Consolidated gross profit was US$176 million, a $152 million improvement over the same quarter 2025. Overall losses for the quarter were in the region of US$833 million.

Net loss attributable to common stockholders for the third quarter was down to US$913 million compared to US$1.173 billion for the same quarter of the prior year, and adjusted net loss per share for the third quarter was US$0.48 compared to US$0.65.

Breaking down the consolidated figures, automotive revenue was US$1.55 billion, a 36% increase over the same quarter of the prior year, including an US$80 million increase in revenues from regulatory credits. Gross profit-loss for the third quarter was a loss of US$80 million down from US$130 million last year.

Revenues from software & services, such as subscription fees, were US$605 million, up 45% on the prior year’s Q3. US$354 million, or 59% of software and services revenue, was attributable to the company’s joint venture with Volkswagen Group. The Group extended Rivian a 10-year loan of US$1 billion in October.

Software and services gross profit for the third quarter was US$256 million, a 42% margin and US$102 million improvement over Q3 2025. Rivian has cited increases in costs for vehicle electrical architecture and software development services from the joint venture with Volkswagen Group and Autonomy+ as behind the rise in the business section's profits.

The Autonomy+ feature allows a degree of autonomous but driver-supervised driving, and the company has announced it is now pursuing a feature named "Point to Point", which will be able to navigate more complex road conditions such as those of urban areas, including road signs and traffic lights, and highway interchanges. The Point to Point feature is slated to be released to all Autonomy+ subscribers next year.

The price of Autonomy+ at present remains at a one-time fee of US$2,500, and the company's Connect+ subscription costs US$15 a month.

The third quarter results show total operating expenses were up, US$1.057 billion compared to US$1.007 billion in the same quarter of 2025. Research and development (R&D) expenses were US$485 million compared to US$453 million in the same period due to increases in software costs. While expenses from sales and general administration remained fairly consistent at US$572 million, this third quarter has seen a loss from operations of US$881 million, down slightly from US$983 million in Q3 2025.

The rise in the company's deliveries this quarter to 19,248 units was largely due to increased sales of its battery electric mid-size SUV, the R2, which outsold the full-size R1 seven-passenger SUV and all-electric delivery van, the EDV, the company says. The R2 was Top Gear's SUV of the Year for 2027, beating the BMW iX3, the Toyota RAV4, Korea's Kia Telluride and fellow US manufacturer Lucid's Gravity.

The removal of the tax credit on EV purchases and the scrapping of emissions standards mean that US auto manufacturers are looking at different ways to make their vehicles attractive to the US buyer. In addition to electric vehicles' single-charge ranges, software-driven autonomous driving features such as Rivian's Autonomy+ are seen as ways that driver and passenger convenience features can be brought to the fore. Ford's electric truck, the Fathom, and Tesla's Cybertruck are capable of acting as power storage devices that can power the owner's home during peak domestic electricity price periods or in the event of grid outage. The potential of such value-adds and the rising cost of fuel at the pumps continue to justify many US manufacturers' policies of keeping a toehold in the EV market in North America.

RJ Scaringe, Rivian founder and CEO, said: "We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter. Customer and media feedback on R2 has been exceptional. Regarding our technology roadmap, our autonomy platform is progressing rapidly, and we are super excited about Point to Point. We are laying the foundations for a future that we believe will be fully electric, autonomous and AI defined. I could not be more excited about the opportunity ahead for Rivian."

title: Garfield Clean Energy column: Overcoming EV uncertainty to realize cost savings
description:
It’s easy to find EV charging stations, especially with tools like the PlugShare app.
On PlugShare, you can locate 77 (and counting) public EV charging stations across six Garfield County municipalities, sporting 135 Level 2 ports and 43 DC Fast ports.
Vehicle range is also a good opportunity to consider your typical vehicle usage.
Fuel cost savings are worth considering in the overall cost of owning an EV.
Mikayla Batts is an intern at Clean Energy Economy for the Region (CLEER), which operates the programs and services of Garfield Clean Energy.
text:
Electric vehicles (EVs) are increasingly common on Colorado roads, but for some prospective buyers, questions remain about what it’s really like to own an EV. The great news is the years following EVs’ initial rollout have provided a wealth of real-world information on the benefits EVs have over traditional gas-powered automobiles.

A longstanding barrier to EV adoption is concerns about the vehicle’s range. In Colorado — and many other states as well — more charging stations are being added frequently. The Colorado Energy Office has been funding charging infrastructure, including expanding high-power Direct Current Fast-Charging (DCFC) along Interstate 70 and Colorado Highway 82 to build out the “Electric Byways” as outlined in their 2023 Colorado Electric Vehicle Plan .

It’s easy to find EV charging stations, especially with tools like the PlugShare app. Lacking the opportunity to install an at-home charger doesn’t mean that owning an EV is impossible. On PlugShare, you can locate 77 (and counting) public EV charging stations across six Garfield County municipalities, sporting 135 Level 2 ports and 43 DC Fast ports.

Vehicle range is also a good opportunity to consider your typical vehicle usage. What is your daily range or commute to work, and how can charging fit into it? Whether it is at the grocery store, work, home or elsewhere, there are plenty of opportunities to keep an EV’s battery topped off and healthy.

The cost of an EV can also factor into the decision-making process of purchasing a vehicle. There are many great incentives available to buy an EV in Colorado. Depending on your income, the Vehicle Exchange Colorado Program (VXC) could be right for you. VXC allows income-qualified Colorado residents to trade in a 12-year-old or older gas vehicle for a rebate of $6,000 for a used EV or $9,000 for a new EV. Additional incentives, like the soon-to-increase state EV tax credit, can also be stacked on VXC for qualifying vehicles.

Fuel cost savings are worth considering in the overall cost of owning an EV. These days, many new EVs cost about the same as their fuel-powered equivalents, but for those with a higher price tag, the EV becomes more affordable when considering the cost of fuel. A light-duty truck or SUV might get 18 miles to the gallon. Compared to an EV with a roughly 250-mile range, you could save nearly $4,000 a year at current fuel prices. There are a variety of online calculators available to compare the cost of your current car with an EV.

A question our team hears sometimes is how EVs perform in Colorado’s cold weather. Cold temperatures can affect an EV’s range or harm its battery, but it is easily managed with a widely available feature called preconditioning. Preconditioning warms up the battery and cabin before you get in. When the EV is plugged in, that energy comes from the grid rather than the battery, and you start the day warm (no more frozen fingers!) without sacrificing range. It also helps with charging: a warm battery accepts a charge more efficiently, and many EVs will precondition automatically while driving if you are navigating towards a fast charger. Even without preconditioning, running seat and steering wheel heating instead of cabin heating can help an EV operate efficiently. Charging stops can also be planned to take place right after driving while the battery is still warm. This helps to preserve driving range and battery health.

Battery health, range anxiety, temperature, and the price of an EV are a couple of considerations that may lie between you and a new ride that’s comfortable and cleaner. Overcoming EV uncertainty can be as simple as thinking through questions and doing some research. Local auto dealers are also another good information source and can help provide real-world insights into what to expect as an EV owner in Garfield County. If the idea of buying an EV is still daunting to you, reach out to CLEER to talk with a ReCharge coach who can help you understand how the tax credits and rebates affect you personally and help you feel comfortable and confident in finding an EV that’s right for you.

Mikayla Batts is an intern at Clean Energy Economy for the Region (CLEER), which operates the programs and services of Garfield Clean Energy. She is a recent graduate of Colorado Mountain College.

This means that means transition credits issued under Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) Program methodology VM0052 Accelerated Retirement of Coal-fired Power Plants Using a Just Transition, v1.1 can now carry the CCP label: the highest benchmark for quality in the carbon markets.
Verra developed VM0052 to tackle one of the hardest problems in climate action: how to close coal plants early in countries where energy security, jobs, and public finances depend on them.
The methodology enables projects to generate transition credits, a new category of credits for the emissions avoided when coal-fired power plants close early and are replaced with clean energy facilities.
It also requires every project to have a just transition plan for affected workers and communities.

title: Mitch McConnell's climate legacy
description:
But the Democrats were never able to put their filibuster-proof majority to work on climate legislation.
The Senate finally passed sweeping climate legislation in 2022, when Democrats enacted the Inflation Reduction Act.
McConnell’s conservative Supreme Court The senator expressed pride in his influence over the Supreme Court.
Both decisions could enable the Supreme Court to block federal climate regulations in the future.
It proved to be a fitting capstone to McConnell’s lengthy career of sabotaging climate policy at every level of government.
text:
Outgoing Sen. Mitch McConnell was one of the most powerful figures ever to walk the halls of the U.S. Congress and was instrumental in steering the country’s climate policy. At virtually every opportunity, he chose to block efforts to address the problem.

McConnell, a Republican from Kentucky, did not seek reelection and is set to retire from the Senate in January. At that point, he will have been the 10th-longest-serving senator in U.S. history. He was also the longest-serving Senate party leader in history.

During his tenure, McConnell exerted his power to halt or overturn climate action in Congress, at the Supreme Court, and in the White House. Over a decades-long career, he joined a short list of individuals most responsible for stymying political efforts to address climate change.

A Senate leader’s war against the president

Over his 40-year tenure in the Senate, McConnell received over $4 million in donations from the oil and gas and coal industries – the fifth-most of any senator.

He was chosen as the leader of Senate Republicans in 2007, shortly before President Barack Obama, a Democrat, won office with a 60-member filibuster-proof Senate majority and a Democratic-controlled House.

At the time, observers thought it possible that Congress would pass bipartisan legislation to combat climate change.

In 2008, Democratic House leader Nancy Pelosi and former Republican House leader Newt Gingrich had created an ad together in which Gingrich said, “We do agree: Our country must take action to address climate change.”

The House soon passed a carbon cap-and-trade bill designed to tackle climate pollution. Eight Republicans voted in favor.

But the Democrats were never able to put their filibuster-proof majority to work on climate legislation. Their majority was thinned by election recounts, legal challenges, member illnesses, the death of Democrat Robert Byrd, and a lost special election in January 2010. What’s more, several Senate Democrats did not support the cap-and-trade bill, so climate advocates needed support from perhaps half a dozen Senate Republicans.

Some Republicans, most prominently the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, worked on a version of the cap-and-trade bill. But rather than support the legislation, McConnell had decided instead to declare war on Obama’s entire agenda, as reporter Ryan Lizza documented in a 2010 article. By working on a climate bill, Republican senators risked angering McConnell.

The cap-and-trade bill died a quiet death, never having received a vote in the Senate.

In 2019, McConnell acknowledged the reality of human-caused climate change. At the time, he said he preferred to solve the problem through technology and innovation. Yet he opposed legislation that climate advocates and researchers said would spur technological innovation, such as a price on carbon pollution and clean energy tax credits.

The Senate finally passed sweeping climate legislation in 2022, when Democrats enacted the Inflation Reduction Act. McConnell vehemently opposed the bill.

In 2025, McConnell helped to repeal many provisions of the Inflation Reduction Act when he supported the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which passed the Senate by a single vote.

McConnell’s conservative Supreme Court

The senator expressed pride in his influence over the Supreme Court. Notably, he blocked Obama’s nomination of moderate Merrick Garland in 2016 to replace Justice Antonin Scalia. In a move that broke with norms and historical precedent, McConnell refused to allow the chamber to consider or vote on Garland’s nomination.

“The most important decision I’ve made in my entire political career was not to fill the Supreme Court vacancy when Justice Scalia passed away,” McConnell recalled in 2024.

Soon after taking office in January 2017, Trump nominated the conservative Neil Gorsuch to the court, and the Republican-controlled Senate approved him. The Senate under McConnell also approved the 2018 nomination of conservative Brett Kavanaugh and the 2020 nomination of conservative Amy Coney Barrett.

The now right-wing court has consistently issued rulings that undermine climate and other environmental regulations.

In the 2022 case West Virginia v. EPA, the court issued a 6-3 decision – with the three new conservative justices in the majority – ruling against the Obama administration’s 2016 Clean Power Plan to regulate climate pollution from power plants. They did so even though the proposed rule never went into effect and by then had already been repealed under the first Trump administration.

In that case, the court also formalized what it called the “major questions doctrine,” which prohibits federal agencies from issuing new regulations that will have major economic or political influence unless Congress has specifically and explicitly delegated that authority.

In the 2024 case Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo, in another 6-3 partisan split, the court overturned the 40-year-old Chevron doctrine, a principle that federal judges should defer to a government agency’s reasonable interpretation of an ambiguous Congressional statute.

Both decisions could enable the Supreme Court to block federal climate regulations in the future.

A crucial vote to acquit

In January 2021, the senator had an opportunity to prevent a second Trump administration. He chose not to take it.

The House of Representatives had impeached Trump for inciting an insurrection at the Capitol a week earlier.

“There’s no question that President Trump is practically and morally responsible for provoking the events of the day,” McConnell said at the time.

But he declined to whip his caucus to remove Trump. Instead, McConnell and 42 other Republican senators voted to acquit him.

Had Trump been impeached, he would have been constitutionally barred from ever again holding office. Instead, he was elected to a second term in 2024 and has presided over the most anti-climate-policy administration in U.S. history, which has included withdrawing from the Paris climate agreement for the second time and repealing virtually all federal climate policies. It proved to be a fitting capstone to McConnell’s lengthy career of sabotaging climate policy at every level of government.

description:
Egypt’s battery-manufacturing ambitions moved forward on 13 September 2026, when BME Battery Manufacturing and China’s CATL signed a contract, witnessed by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, to establish an electric-battery plant.
What Is Driving Egypt’s Battery Manufacturing Push?
Egypt’s planned battery projects cover different stages of the battery value chain, from battery-pack assembly to cell manufacturing and stationary energy-storage systems.
In Egypt, it is partnering with BME on a battery manufacturing project, providing technology licensing, production equipment, battery cells and technical training.
BME Battery Manufacturing Headquarters: Egypt Established by Egyptian automotive companies MCV and Auto D, BME is developing a battery manufacturing plant in partnership with CATL.
text:
Egypt has announced a series of battery-manufacturing and energy-storage projects in 2026, led by a BME–CATL plant targeting 1 GWh of annual capacity and a US$200 million Kemet–Cornex storage-battery facility planned at 5 GWh. Together they link electric mobility with renewable-energy storage.

Egypt’s battery-manufacturing ambitions moved forward on 13 September 2026, when BME Battery Manufacturing and China’s CATL signed a contract, witnessed by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, to establish an electric-battery plant. The project carries an initial investment above EGP 2 billion, about US$39 million, and a first-phase capacity of 1 GWh a year, with batteries for heavy commercial vehicles as the initial focus.

The agreement forms part of a broader series of developments announced in 2026. In January, Kemet Industries agreed to a US$200 million energy-storage battery facility with a Chinese technology partner. In June, AMEA Power and its partners signed contracts covering 1,500 MWh of storage projects and a separate factory designed to produce 3,000 MWh of storage systems annually. Sungrow broke ground on a storage-systems plant with planned annual capacity of 10 GWh in August, while Mansour Group and Tianneng signed a memorandum of understanding in September to explore battery-manufacturing opportunities.

These developments connect two markets: batteries for electric mobility and battery systems for renewable-energy storage. The projects remain at different stages, ranging from signed agreements and construction starts to exploratory partnerships.

What Is Driving Egypt’s Battery Manufacturing Push?

Two policy priorities are supporting Egypt’s battery-manufacturing ambitions. In the automotive sector, the National Automotive Industry Development Programme aims to raise local value-added content to 60 per cent, strengthen domestic component production and attract international manufacturers. Industry Minister Khaled Hashem described the BME–CATL agreement as a step towards developing local battery capabilities as demand grows for electric vehicles and energy-storage technologies.

In the power sector, battery storage can help integrate renewable electricity and improve grid flexibility. Egypt commissioned its first utility-scale battery energy-storage system, a 300 MWh facility connected to the 500 MW Abydos solar plant in Aswan, in July 2025. The government subsequently announced a target of 14,320 MWh of battery-storage capacity, with official reports citing both 2028 and 2029 as the deadline. AMEA Power’s two contracted projects total 1,500 MWh, equivalent to approximately 10.5 per cent of that target; the comparison reflects planned project capacity, not completed national progress.

How Does the BME–CATL Partnership Support Local Production?

BME (Battery Manufacturing Egypt) was established by commercial-vehicle manufacturer MCV and Auto D. The contract was signed by BME chairman Maged Wahib and CATL international investment director Luo Haining. CATL will provide battery technology licensing, production equipment and training, while BME builds and funds the plant and sources battery cells from CATL.

The first phase targets 1 GWh a year for heavy commercial vehicles. A second phase would lift capacity to 5 GWh, five times the initial level, and extend into passenger-car batteries and storage systems for solar and wind power. The project targets 40 % local content, covering assembly, battery-management-system integration, thermal management and final system integration in Egypt, and it is planned to serve domestic and international markets. Prime Minister Madbouly said the government wants to accelerate implementation and move quickly to the next executive steps.

How Are Battery-Cell Manufacturing and Systems Assembly Developing?

Egypt’s planned battery projects cover different stages of the battery value chain, from battery-pack assembly to cell manufacturing and stationary energy-storage systems. The BME–CATL partnership will use CATL-supplied cells for locally assembled battery packs, while Sungrow and AMEA Power are advancing storage-system manufacturing plans. The Kemet–Cornex agreement adds another stage through a proposed US$200 million battery-cell facility targeting an annual capacity of 5,000 MWh (5 GWh). The project also aims to use locally sourced materials and components while transferring manufacturing technology to Egypt.

Announced in January 2026 during Electricity Minister Mahmoud Esmat’s visit to China, the Kemet agreement formed part of a broader US$700 million investment package, including a separate US$500 million solar-cell manufacturing complex involving GCL Group. Together, these projects reflect Egypt’s efforts to expand domestic renewable-energy equipment production, attract international investment and develop technical capabilities through technology partnerships. Their eventual contribution will depend on implementation, production timelines and the extent of local manufacturing.

Which Projects Are Expanding Renewable-Energy Storage?

On 4 June 2026, AMEA Power and its partners signed engineering, procurement and construction contracts for two standalone battery energy-storage projects: the 500 MWh Horus project in Zafarana and the 1,000 MWh Nefertiti project in Benban, Aswan. Together, they will provide 1,500 MWh of planned storage capacity. The agreements also covered a separate factory involving AMEA Power, China Energy and Gotion, with planned annual production capacity of 3,000 MWh of storage systems. In July, Egypt’s Cabinet approved golden licences for the Horus and Nefertiti projects, which represent combined investments of US$800 million, including US$450 million for Nefertiti and US$350 million for Horus.

Sungrow broke ground on 17 August 2026 on a US$50 million factory in the TEDA industrial zone within the Suez Canal Economic Zone’s Sokhna Industrial Zone. The facility will assemble battery energy-storage systems and targets an annual capacity of 10 GWh, with production expected to begin in April 2027. Its planned output will support Egypt’s domestic storage market, including the Energy Valley project in Minya, which is designed to combine 1.95 GW of solar generation with 3.9 GWh of battery storage. These projects could strengthen Egypt’s renewable-energy infrastructure while expanding local manufacturing capabilities, subject to construction progress and commissioning schedules.

Mansour–Tianneng Partnership Explores Egypt’s Next Phase of Battery Manufacturing

Mansour Group and Tianneng Battery Group signed a memorandum of understanding on 2 September 2026, witnessed by Investment Minister Mohamed Farid Saleh, to assess the feasibility of producing lead-acid batteries for automobiles and lithium batteries for new-energy vehicles in Egypt. Tianneng has about 40 years of experience, ranks first in China in lead-acid battery production and works across lead-acid, lithium-ion, sodium-ion and solid-state technologies. The MoU was signed during President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Egypt and aligns with the automotive programme’s local value-added goals. As a feasibility study, it widens the technology options available to Egypt’s automotive and storage sectors.

How Could Supply Chains and Trade Benefit?

Local battery production brings battery systems closer to Egyptian vehicle makers. CATL said BME’s use of its technology will allow direct supply to local automakers, filling a gap in domestic battery-pack manufacturing.

Export potential also features in the plans. BME’s battery systems are intended for domestic and international markets, and Sungrow’s Sokhna location within the Suez Canal Economic Zone offers access to Red Sea and Suez Canal shipping routes for regional supply.

What Opportunities and Milestones Lie Ahead?

Electric mobility: BME plans to begin with battery packs for heavy commercial vehicles before expanding into passenger-vehicle batteries and energy-storage systems.

Grid storage: AMEA Power’s two projects represent 1,500 MWh of planned storage capacity, against Egypt’s national target of 14,320 MWh by 2029.

Local value added: A 40 per cent local-content target at BME, and technology transfer under the Kemet–Cornex plan.

Skills and employment: CATL will provide training to BME, and Sungrow’s plant is expected to create more than 100 direct jobs.

Upcoming milestones: Key developments to monitor include the BME plant’s location and construction schedule, progress on the Kemet–Krenex facility, and construction and commissioning updates for the announced storage projects.

Key Statistics

EGP 2 billion+ (about US$39 million): Initial investment in the BME–CATL plant.

1 GWh to 5 GWh: Planned annual capacity across the BME–CATL first and second phases.

40 per cent: Target local-content share for the BME–CATL project.

US$200 million and 5,000 MWh: Kemet–Cornex investment and planned annual capacity.

1,500 MWh: Combined capacity of AMEA Power’s Horus (500 MWh) and Nefertiti (1,000 MWh) projects.

3,000 MWh: Planned annual capacity of the AMEA Power–Gotion–China Energy storage-systems factory.

US$50 million and 10 GWh: Sungrow’s investment and planned annual capacity in Sokhna.

14,320 MWh: Egypt’s target for battery-storage capacity under its 2026–2029 renewable-energy strategy.

Top 5 Companies Advancing Egypt’s Battery Industry

Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Limited (CATL)

Headquarters: Ningde, Fujian, China

CATL is a leading global battery technology and manufacturing company. In Egypt, it is partnering with BME on a battery manufacturing project, providing technology licensing, production equipment, battery cells and technical training. The initial phase will focus on battery systems for heavy commercial vehicles, with planned expansion into passenger-vehicle batteries and renewable-energy storage.

BME Battery Manufacturing

Headquarters: Egypt

Established by Egyptian automotive companies MCV and Auto D, BME is developing a battery manufacturing plant in partnership with CATL. The project targets initial annual production capacity of 1 GWh, with a planned second phase increasing capacity to 5 GWh. It also aims for 40 per cent local content, supporting domestic manufacturing capabilities and potential export opportunities.

Kemet Industries Group

Headquarters: Egypt

Kemet Industries has signed an agreement with a Chinese technology partner for a planned US$200 million energy-storage battery-cell manufacturing facility. The project targets annual production capacity of 5,000 MWh and aims to localise manufacturing technology and use locally sourced raw materials.

Sungrow

Headquarters: Hefei, Anhui, China

Sungrow began construction in August 2026 on a US$50 million battery energy-storage systems assembly plant in Egypt’s Suez Canal Economic Zone. The facility targets annual capacity of 10 GWh, with production expected to begin in April 2027.

AMEA Power

Headquarters: Dubai, United Arab Emirates

Part of Al Nowais Group, AMEA Power is advancing two standalone battery energy-storage projects in Egypt: Horus, with 500 MWh of capacity, and Nefertiti, with 1,000 MWh. The projects have a combined planned storage capacity of 1,500 MWh. A separate partnership involving AMEA Power, China Energy and Gotion also covers a planned factory with annual production capacity of 3,000 MWh of energy-storage systems.

Conclusion

Egypt’s battery-manufacturing industry is developing across two connected markets: electric mobility and renewable-energy storage. The BME–CATL agreement, Kemet’s planned battery-cell facility, AMEA Power’s storage projects, Sungrow’s manufacturing investment and the Mansour–Tianneng feasibility study reflect growing international cooperation to expand domestic production and transfer technology. However, these initiatives remain at different stages, and their long-term impact will depend on implementation, local sourcing, technical capabilities and market demand. As projects advance, their progress will help determine how effectively Egypt can build a competitive battery supply chain, support renewable-energy integration and strengthen its automotive manufacturing sector.

description:

Domestic battery component production costs are reportedly 18–61% higher than China’s.
India Plans ₹12,000-Crore Battery Component Scheme as Industry Seeks 50% Subsidy to Compete With China New Delhi, November 3: India’s battery manufacturing industry is seeking capital subsidies of up to 50% as the government prepares a proposed ₹12,000-crore incentive scheme to strengthen domestic production of advanced battery components.
The government has targeted 50 GWh of domestic battery manufacturing capacity under the existing programme.

text:
Indian battery component manufacturers are seeking substantial government support to overcome production costs that are reportedly 18–61% higher than China’s and strengthen the domestic electric vehicle supply chain.

Highlights

India is planning a ₹12,000-crore battery component manufacturing scheme.

Industry players are seeking capital subsidies of up to 50%.

Domestic battery component production costs are reportedly 18–61% higher than China’s.

The proposed incentives aim to attract investment in local manufacturing.

The initiative could reduce India’s dependence on imported battery materials and components.

Stronger domestic supply chains could support electric vehicles and energy storage industries.

India Plans ₹12,000-Crore Battery Component Scheme as Industry Seeks 50% Subsidy to Compete With China

New Delhi, November 3: India’s battery manufacturing industry is seeking capital subsidies of up to 50% as the government prepares a proposed ₹12,000-crore incentive scheme to strengthen domestic production of advanced battery components. The move aims to reduce dependence on Chinese imports and support India’s expanding electric vehicle and energy storage industries.

According to a Moneycontrol report published on November 2, the proposed scheme is currently under inter-ministerial consultation. Industry representatives have highlighted substantial cost disadvantages faced by Indian manufacturers compared with Chinese suppliers. Moneycontrol +1

Indian Battery Components Cost Up to 61% More

A report prepared by the Net-Zero Energy Transition Association (NETRA), in collaboration with IIT Madras and industry stakeholders, estimates that manufacturing battery components in India costs 18–61% more than importing comparable products from China.

The cost difference varies across components. Lithium iron phosphate cathode materials are estimated to cost 47% more, while nickel manganese cobalt cathode materials carry an 18% disadvantage. Natural and synthetic graphite anode materials are 51% and 61% more expensive, respectively.

Higher capital investment requirements, limited manufacturing scale and supply chain constraints contribute to the competitiveness gap. Moneycontrol

Industry Proposes Three Subsidy Models

Battery manufacturers have proposed three incentive structures to help establish a competitive domestic ecosystem.

The first combines a 25% capital expenditure subsidy with component-specific operating incentives. The second relies entirely on operational subsidies, while the third proposes capital subsidies of up to 50%, linked to actual investments.

Industry stakeholders have also recommended linking government support to domestic value addition, production capacity and sales performance.

Battery Demand Could Reach 236 GWh by 2032

India’s battery demand is projected to increase from 33 gigawatt-hours (GWh) in 2025 to 236 GWh by 2032 and nearly 600 GWh by 2037.

However, domestic component manufacturing capacity remains significantly below projected requirements.

The proposed scheme would support essential materials, including cathodes, anodes, electrolytes, separators and current collector foils.

Existing ₹18,100-Crore PLI Scheme

The proposed programme would complement India’s existing ₹18,100-crore Production Linked Incentive scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries.

The government has targeted 50 GWh of domestic battery manufacturing capacity under the existing programme. Of this, 40 GWh has already been awarded to four companies. Press Information Bureau

What Happens Next?

The proposed ₹12,000-crore scheme could help attract investments, develop domestic suppliers and strengthen India’s position in the global battery supply chain.

However, the subsidy structure, eligibility conditions and final financial allocation remain subject to government approval.

title: Electric aviation is taking off in unexpected ways - Grist
description:
The call came from a home in Hyde County, a rural expanse of coastal farmland and marsh in North Carolina.
Paramedic Quinn Reece jumped into an electric aircraft with one seat, two wings, and eight propellers.
These developments point to a fast-approaching future for electric aviation.
Emergency response is one avenue where electric aviation is beginning to find a practical use.
“Vertical flight is inherently energy-intensive, and an electric aircraft is not necessarily more energy-efficient or lower-carbon per passenger-mile than an electric car, bus, or train,” he said.
text:
The call came from a home in Hyde County, a rural expanse of coastal farmland and marsh in North Carolina. Paramedic Quinn Reece jumped into an electric aircraft with one seat, two wings, and eight propellers. It is called a BlackFly, and at about 14 feet long it looks like an oversized drone. Moments later it rose like a helicopter, then flew like an airplane.

As she raced toward the emergency at about 60 mph, a dispatcher described the location. Reece quickly realized that the app the county uses for emergency response had given the wrong location. Because she had flown over the area before, Reece had an idea of the correct location. She zipped over in the aircraft, confirmed where the call had come from, and relayed the information to paramedics headed that way. She was on the scene and administering care 20 minutes before they arrived.

That is exactly what Brook Cox, the county’s emergency medical services chief, hoped to see. She launched the six-month trial with a company called Pivotal in March to see if its BlackFly could help medics more quickly reach patients in a county that covers 1,459 square miles of land and water. The county conducted more than 300 training flights prior to using the aircraft for two 911 calls.

Air taxis and flying cars have long defined the promise of electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, or eVTOLs. This is the vision the Federal Aviation Administration has highlighted through the eVTOL Integration Pilot Program, which works with manufacturers to test the emerging aircraft in real-world settings. Last week, Archer Aviation announced plans for aerial taxi services in three Texas cities and Joby Aviation began demonstrations in Florida.

Hyde County is among those exploring more immediate uses for these machines. The FAA program considers emergency medical response an important application, particularly in rural areas. Similar aircraft powered by the sun that can stay aloft for weeks are being developed to monitor climate threats like wildfires, methane emissions and ice melt.

The great promise of electric aviation is to help decarbonize flight. These developments point to a fast-approaching future for electric aviation. It just might not arrive in the form we expected.

Kristina Menton, Pivotal’s vice president of flight, points to a December 2024 flight as proof the technology could be a boon to EMS. A BlackFly took off from a Los Angeles County fire station and landed in a backyard in Malibu, demonstrating it could fly directly to a private address.

Menton acknowledged that single-seater aircraft are a new approach for a field that has typically employed separate crews for flight and EMS operations. BlackFly’s simplified controls allow one person to serve as both pilot and medic. “The aircraft is a breeze,” Cox said. “It really takes the guesswork out of it because you have a screen and you have all these prompts that you have to go through.”

Carl Dietrich, who founded Jump Aero in 2019 to build electric aircraft for EMS, sees Pivotal’s work as proof of concept rather than competition, something that can only help the sector grow. “It shows that other organizations believe that this is a real opportunity,” he said.

Jump Aero is building a different kind of aircraft, the JA1 Pulse, which has been in development for seven years. Dietrich expects it to reach 288 mph, compared with 63 mph for the BlackFly. He said eVTOLs aren’t necessarily replacing helicopters or ambulances, but adding something new to emergency response: an aircraft that is easy to fly and can launch almost immediately without warming up.

“It’s ideal for rapid response missions because you don’t pay any maintenance penalty for going to full power instantly,” he said. This is particularly important in a field that aims to arrive within eight minutes of a call, while rural response times average nearly 15 minutes.

There are, of course, limitations, including battery range and weight capacity. The BlackFly can travel 20 miles on a charge and carry 200 pounds, while the JA1 Pulse is good for 70 miles and 350 pounds. The aircraft clearly aren’t meant to transport patients; their utility lies in being able to quickly reach an emergency and stabilize a patient until an ambulance arrives. Reece carried a cardiac monitor, airway supplies, and a “primary response bag” of essential gear that would allow her to assess a patient and begin treatment immediately.

Rural areas may present an easier path to introducing the technology, said April Zhang, director of advanced air mobility at the University of South Florida’s Center for Urban Transportation Research. “In the urban area, it’s probably more challenging to find the right landing and takeoff sites,” she said. Menton said other counties are already looking at Hyde County’s experience and considering similar programs.

Zhang points to the eVTOL Integration Pilot Program as a way for manufacturers and public agencies to collaborate on applications. Beyond EMS, she sees traffic surveillance and cargo deliveries as other potential uses.

FAA policy may also give public agencies an easier path to using eVTOLs than commercial operators. Andrew Mearns, a commercialization consultant at Multicopter Aerospace Consulting, said EMS organizations can often operate under the FAA’s public aircraft rules, which could allow them to fly without the credentials required of a commercial pilot.

Cost is another appeal. Pivotal’s model sells for $190,000, while Mearns said helicopters can cost from $500,000 to $10 million. Operating costs will vary with the specific model, but generally speaking an electric aircraft will be about 20 percent cheaper than a similarly sized machine that burns fossil fuels, Mearns said.

Emergency response is one avenue where electric aviation is beginning to find a practical use. Another is taking shape much higher in the atmosphere.

Unmanned stratospheric aircraft can reach altitudes of 65,000 feet, about twice as high as commercial aircraft. Solar-powered versions can remain aloft for weeks or months, making them well suited to long-term environmental monitoring.

“If you imagine these solar-powered aircraft just circling the L.A. County area, collecting soil moisture, vegetation moisture data, with complex math models and deep learning mapped to that, you can have improved risk profiles better than the models that are currently there,” said Craig Mascarenhas, an aerospace researcher at Harvard University. The aircraft could also spot fires more quickly and help map them for first responders.

Mascarenhas leads engineering research for Harvard’s branch of the Stratospheric Airborne Climate Observing System, where he is helping develop and deploy solar-powered electric aircraft with Electra.Aero, MIT and others. He said their applications go beyond wildfires.

“It’s hurricane monitoring and tracking, methane emiss monitoring, understanding ice dynamics across the world,” he said. “The instruments will be swapped, but the topology of the aircraft will remain the same.”

The aircraft themselves could offer environmental benefits too. Mascarenhas said eVTOLs could reduce greenhouse gas emissions when they replace fuel-burning helicopters, but the climate case is less clear when they replace efficient ground transportation.

“Vertical flight is inherently energy-intensive, and an electric aircraft is not necessarily more energy-efficient or lower-carbon per passenger-mile than an electric car, bus, or train,” he said.

For Pivotal, EMS in Hyde County is just the beginning. Menton said the company’s broader vision is to “revolutionize transportation” by making short electric flights accessible to more people.

But for now, some of the technology’s most immediate uses may be the specialized applications already being tested in places like Hyde County and high above it.

text:
US power-sector emissions are going to increase 42% by 2030, as planned data centers switched on.

A new analysis by the Sierra Club, reported by Bloomberg, finds that if planned AI data centers are built, the US power sector would emit about 2.1 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide in 2030.

That is 618 million tons more than in 2025, roughly a 42% jump, enough to undo 15 years' worth of emissions cuts from US electricity. The biggest driver is “bring-your-own-power” plants built on site for data centers, mostly burning natural gas, which alone could emit more than 460 million tons a year, about as much as all of Mexico.

US electricity emissions peaked in 2007 and have fallen since, as coal plants closed and wind and solar grew. The Sierra Club's own experts say the numbers “continue to sort of boggle our minds,” and their estimate is several times higher than what they projected just 18 months ago.

Other groups project smaller rises, and some energy analysts say many announced projects may never get built, so this is one advocacy group's projection, not a certainty.

source: Roston, E., & Raimonde, O. (2026, October 29). New data centers projected to emit more carbon than all of Mexico. Bloomberg.

title: Europe must build its hydrogen market - European Investment Bank
description:
Europe has laid the foundations for a clean hydrogen market.
For the European Investment Bank, the market is entering a crucial new phase.
Incentives for clean hydrogen demand, dedicated financing schemes and plans for new infrastructure further strengthen the investment environment.
Clean hydrogen is heavily influenced by electricity prices, which typically account for most hydrogen production costs In several applications, clean hydrogen remains materially more expensive than fossil-based alternatives, requiring policy support, carbon pricing or customers willing to pay a green premium.
The project shows how clean hydrogen can be integrated directly into existing industrial processes today, replacing fossil-based hydrogen and enabling the future deployment of low-carbon fuels.
text:
Europe has laid the foundations for a clean hydrogen market. The next step is coordinated investment in production, industrial applications and the infrastructure needed to connect supply with demand.

This is essential if clean hydrogen is to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, strengthen energy security and decarbonize industries where direct electrification is difficult.

For the European Investment Bank, the market is entering a crucial new phase. It is moving from announcements to investment decisions and targeted delivery.

Networks, pipelines and storage should be developed gradually, in line with proven demand and initially around industrial clusters, to avoid overcapacity and stranded assets. The priority, therefore, is pragmatic execution: converting public support and planned projects into bankable investments backed by credible buyers and measurable decarbonization impact.

Europe combines a large project pipeline, a manufacturing base and strong policy support. The International Energy Agency estimates that Europe will install around 80% of the worldwide electrolyser capacity expected to come online in 2026.

Europe also accounts for a fifth of global electrolyzer manufacturing capacity, with higher-performance designs and room to grow. Incentives for clean hydrogen demand, dedicated financing schemes and plans for new infrastructure further strengthen the investment environment.

Clean hydrogen is heavily influenced by electricity prices, which typically account for most hydrogen production costs

In several applications, clean hydrogen remains materially more expensive than fossil-based alternatives, requiring policy support, carbon pricing or customers willing to pay a green premium. As a result, demand uncertainty and limited bankable offtake agreements are the main barriers to scaling up the sector.

Despite these challenges, clean hydrogen remains particularly relevant where electricity cannot easily be used directly. It can replace hydrogen made from fossil fuels in fertilizer production, chemicals and refining, while also helping to decarbonize steel, heavy transport and other hard-to-abate industries.

Clean hydrogen is part of the European Investment Bank’s broader support for the energy transition. In 2025, the EIB Group provided €33 billion for Europe's energy security, spanning renewables, electricity grids, energy efficiency and clean technologies such as hydrogen.

Over the past five years, the European Investment Bank has approved around €2 billion1directly linked to the clean hydrogen value chain, covering projects ranging from electrolyzer technologies and hydrogen production to refuelling infrastructure, hydrogen-powered transport and renewable fuels. These operations reflect the growing range of applications in the hydrogen economy.

Recent European Investment Bank financing for energy and chemicals company OMV's flagship clean hydrogen project in Austria illustrates the shift from ambition to implementation. The project shows how clean hydrogen can be integrated directly into existing industrial processes today, replacing fossil-based hydrogen and enabling the future deployment of low-carbon fuels.

The European Investment Bank has also financed Iberdrola’s 20 MW electrolyzer supplying clean hydrogen to a fertilizer plant in Spain and Galp’s 100 MW electrolyzer for advanced biofuel production in Portugal.

Together, projects like these are helping build experience, scale and confidence across Europe's emerging hydrogen market.

The turnaround is bolstered by data center demand for energy storage, but was anchored by the US stationary storage market, where Samsung SDI said it secured more than 60 GWh of ESS battery orders in 2026.
That tally includes a 1 GWh US supply agreement with Alpha Omega Power for its nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) Samsung Battery Box 1.7 and a US cell supply arrangement with Sungrow.

text:
Samsung SDI posted its highest quarterly operating profit in three years in the third quarter of 2026, driven by utility-scale energy storage system (ESS) orders and battery backup units (BBUs) for artificial intelligence data centers.

Revenue rose 52.6% year-on-year, with operating profit reaching KRW 407.8 billion (USD 304 million) after an operating loss a year earlier. The battery division generated KRW 4.41 trillion in revenue (USD 3.28 billion), up 55.3% year-on-year, and posted a KRW 361.9 billion (USD 269 million) operating profit.

The turnaround is bolstered by data center demand for energy storage, but was anchored by the US stationary storage market, where Samsung SDI said it secured more than 60 GWh of ESS battery orders in 2026. That tally includes a 1 GWh US supply agreement with Alpha Omega Power for its nickel cobalt aluminum (NCA) Samsung Battery Box 1.7 and a US cell supply arrangement with Sungrow.

The South Korean-headquartered company said that, as part of its two-track NCA and LFP chemistry strategy, it began mass production of LFP cells in October at its StarPlus Energy facility in Indiana.

US electric vehicle demand remains slow enough that factories meant to supply cells and packs for mobility purposes are not as viable as when investment decisions were made.

Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solutions have both pivoted factory lines towards LFP for stationary storage, and Samsung said it is designating its Synergy Cells plant in Indiana as an ESS production hub, and further accelerating EV-to-LFP line conversions in the fourth quarter. LG did similar with its own JV with Stellantis.

To avoid Chinese import tariffs and meet Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) rules, it said it has “signed long-term supply agreements for LFP cathode materials with major Korean materials companies to meet U.S. demand for supply chains independent of China.”

Samsung SDI also recently launched cylindrical LFP cells for data center BBUs and aims to close additional long-term utility-scale ESS and uninterruptible power supply (UPS) contracts before year-end, alongside bidding in South Korea’s third government-led ESS procurement round.
